column1: # THE PARITY LEDGER -- known TypeScript/Go divergences. THIS FILE SHOULD
# NORMALLY BE EMPTY OF ROWS.
# test/spec/*.tsv is the contract: a row lives there only once BOTH
# implementations satisfy it. This file is the debt register for the
# opposite case -- a behaviour where the two ports are known to DISAGREE,
# recorded so the disagreement is visible and tracked instead of being
# rediscovered, and so nobody baselines one engine's output as the shared
# contract by accident.
# It is deliberately a .tsv living beside the suite, so it is read
# whenever the spec is read. Both runners (ts/test/spec.test.ts and
# go/spec_test.go) glob test/spec/*.tsv and skip comment and blank lines,
# so a file of comments contributes zero rows and asserts nothing.
# HOW TO USE IT
# A divergence is a BUG, not a feature. The default response is to fix
# the engine, not to write here. Add an entry ONLY when the divergence
# cannot be fixed from this repository right now -- e.g. it originates in
# a pinned @tabnas dependency, or the correct behaviour is an open
# language-design question.
# An entry MUST carry:
#   1. an issue reference (the tracking issue for the fix), and
#   2. a reason it is not simply fixed, and
#   3. the exact divergent inputs and BOTH engines' outputs.
# An entry is removed -- not amended -- when the divergence is fixed, and
# the behaviour then earns real rows in the appropriate spec file.
# Entries carry NO data rows: a row here would be executed by both
# runners and, by definition, could not pass in both. Everything below is
# commentary.
# NOTE (2026-08-11): five entries were RECLASSIFIED from DIVERGENCE.md
# by maintainer decision -- previously accepted as permanent, now debt
# to be fixed; only the Unicode table vintage remains there. Three are
# already fixed and removed (#29 message text, #30 parse-level canon,
# #31 invalid-source stages); the surrogate (#24) and malformed-input
# (#32) entries below remain, blocked on upstream @tabnas work and a
# direction decision.
# OPEN -- lone surrogates in quoted strings folded to U+FFFD by Go.
#   issue: #24 (REOPENED 2026-08-11; the 2026-08-11 decision to accept
#   this permanently is reversed -- parity is required). Go conflates
#   values TS keeps distinct, breaking the lattice law that two
#   different values never unify; as map keys it silently merges
#   distinct entries.
#   Divergent input:  x:"\ud800" x:"�"
#   TypeScript: error, Cannot unify values at $.x (values distinct)
#   Go:         SUCCESS, {"x":"�"} (values conflated)
#   Not simply fixed because the fold happens at LEX time in the
#   pinned @tabnas/parser Go lexer (deliberate upstream, matching
#   encoding/json), and the direction is undecided: refuse unpaired
#   surrogates in BOTH ports (restores the law, removes a working TS
#   capability) or preserve in both (upstream lexer change + Go
#   emission path). The upstream per-port pinning tests assert
#   OPPOSITE results on purpose and must flip together with the fix.
#   Paired forms all agree and keep their real rows (scalar.tsv
#   surrogate-*).
# OPEN -- an include CYCLE is reported at a different site, with a
#   different path spelling, and with the chain rendered in TS only.
#   issue: none filed yet; found 2026-08-27 while landing the module
#   distribution fixes (use-cases/REVIEW.md finding H). NOT introduced
#   by that work -- it reproduces on a plain two-file include cycle with
#   no modules involved, and is recorded here because the modself
#   fixture now reaches the guard that exposes it.
#   Divergent input:  a.aon `x: @"b.aon"`, b.aon `y: @"b.aon"` `z: @"a.aon"`
#   TypeScript: [aontu/multisource_cycle] at b.aon:1:4, naming the
#               RESOLVED path (/tmp/cyc/b.aon), hint chain rendered
#               `/tmp/cyc/b.aon -> /tmp/cyc/b.aon`
#   Go:         [aontu/multisource_cycle] at a.aon:1:4, naming the
#               SPELLING (b.aon), hint chain rendered as the literal
#               `{loop}` -- the placeholder is never filled
#   Both refuse, with the same code and the same exit class, so the
#   disagreement is in the diagnostic and not in the verdict.
#   Not simply fixed because all three differences originate in the
#   pinned @tabnas/multisource (0.5.2, both ports): the code, the
#   message, the blamed site and the `{loop}` hint placeholder are the
#   dependency's, not this repository's. Two of the three are arguably
#   upstream BUGS rather than choices -- an unfilled `{loop}` says
#   nothing to the reader it was written for, and naming the resolved
#   absolute path contradicts the site rule finding F established for
#   every finding this repo does own (a site prints the file as the
#   entry's own spelling reaches it, so a SARIF upload stays
#   repo-relative). Fixing it means an upstream change in both ports of
#   multisource, released together.
#   No spec row asserts any of it: `mod-nested-has-its-own-root` pins
#   the CLASS (errc -> syntax), which both ports agree on.
# CLOSED 2026-08-27 -- a finding's site names the WRONG FILE under an
#   `@"..."` include, in Go.
#   issue: #66 (recorded 2026-08-24, from the 2026-08-21 status
#   report's section 4).
#   CLOSED by the site-attribution invariant (use-cases/REVIEW.md
#   finding F, BUGS.md §25): Go's include resolver now stamps the
#   RESOLVED path onto every Val a loaded document parses into
#   (`aonProcessor`/`stampResolved`, go/source.go) and keeps that
#   document's text so the offsets can be resolved in the right file
#   (`Aontu.IncludeText`), which is exactly the "carry the source URL
#   down the include path" sweep this entry said was owed. TypeScript
#   stopped OVERWRITING the loaded url with the entry's in the same
#   change, so the two ports met rather than one moving to the other.
#   The fixture below now reports `part.aon:1:7` from BOTH ports,
#   byte-identical through `--format json`. Kept as a note because the
#   opposite-direction warning about #76 still holds.
#   What it used to do: The row and column are right; only the file
#   is wrong, which is the dangerous shape: an agent applying a patch
#   from sites[].file + row + col edits that position in a file the
#   constraint was never written in.
#   Divergent input:  part.aon `port: integer`, main.aon
#   `@"./part.aon"` + `name: string`, data `{"port":"eighty"}`;
#   `aontu vet main.aon data.json --format json`.
#   TypeScript: schema site file = .../part.aon, row 1, col 7
#   Go:         schema site file = main.aon,     row 1, col 7
#   (col 7 of main.aon is inside the include directive itself.)
#   Why it stood as long as it did: the two ports carried a loaded
#   file's identity differently. TS threaded the resolved URL onto
#   every Val parsed from it, where the Go port kept the ENTRY
#   document's URL on the context and stamped it at finding time.
#   Making Go match meant carrying the source URL down the include path
#   onto each Val -- the same sweep `setPaths` needed for constraints
#   (register, G1 phase 4), and worth doing as its own change rather
#   than inside a release fix. It was done as one, and it also settled
#   what a report should CALL such a file: the resolved absolute path
#   is the right identity and the wrong name, so a site prints the file
#   as the entry's own spelling reaches it (`displayFile`), which is
#   what keeps a SARIF upload repo-relative.
#   SEE ALSO the #76 entry below: the same machinery seen from the other
#   side. This entry is a value that HAS a document and is attributed to
#   the wrong one; that one is a value that has NO document and is
#   attributed to one anyway. Same cause -- Go keeps the entry URL on
#   the context and stamps it at finding time -- and fixing this one
#   does not settle that one.
#   THE FIXES POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which is why flattening the
#   two into "Go names a file TypeScript does not" is worse than not
#   summarising them at all: THIS entry needs the loaded document's url
#   CARRIED FURTHER, onto every Val parsed from it, while #76 needs
#   attribution WITHHELD. A reader who took the flattened form would
#   fix this one by clearing the file, which is precisely wrong --
#   TypeScript names part.aon here, and is right to.
# CLOSED -- malformed-input acceptance edges and invalid-UTF-8
#   replacement counts. issue: #32. Every input this entry recorded now
#   gets the same verdict from both engines. Kept as a note because the
#   two halves closed for quite different reasons, and because the
#   acceptance half closed WITHOUT the upstream fix it was waiting for.
#   Invalid UTF-8 was a staging error, not a disagreement. Node replaces
#   invalid bytes as it DECODES a file, so the canonical engine never saw
#   one; Go carried them to the JSON encoder, which replaced them per
#   byte at the very end. Hence one U+FFFD against two for a truncated
#   E2 82 -- and, unrecorded here, `�` escapes against the character
#   itself, which no gens row could have held. Replacing at decode fixed
#   both, and fixed them for every stage in between: lexer, parser, canon
#   and error frames now see the text the canonical engine sees. Pinned
#   by per-port twins over a byte fixture (test/spec/files/
#   invalid-utf8.aon), exactly as this entry predicted it would have to
#   be, since the src column cannot carry raw invalid bytes.
#   The acceptance edges -- `pref(1-3)`, `close(([]%))`, `1'00]`,
#   `"q k""?:1` -- were expected to need an upstream @tabnas change,
#   because which shapes the grammar admits is decided there. They did
#   not. Two of them were TypeScript CRASHES (#49): a raw parse value
#   reaching a func's peg, and a grouping paren's raw array reaching
#   addsite. Converting at the paren handler, which the Go port had
#   always done, settled `close(([]%))` outright. `pref(1-3)` then
#   settled as a wrong ARGUMENT COUNT once arity was checked (#51). The
#   remaining two agree on the verdict and differ only in trailing
#   context lines, which is a renderer difference tracked by #50.
#   The lesson worth keeping: "upstream" was the diagnosis for four
#   inputs, and was right about none of them. The parser stacks may well
#   still differ on shapes nobody has written down -- but a fuzz finding
#   that proves it would be a NEW entry with its own inputs, not this
#   one, which no longer records a divergence anyone can reproduce.
#   Well-formed sources were unaffected throughout.
# CLOSED -- lone surrogates in quoted strings folded to U+FFFD by Go.
#   issue: #24. Two separate things lived under this entry; both are
#   settled, in opposite ways, and the difference is the point.
#   The BRACED-SPELLING half was a plain upstream BUG. The pair lookahead
#   in @tabnas/parser's Go lexer sat inside the 4-hex escape branch and
#   recognised only its own spelling, while the braced branch wrote its
#   rune immediately with no lookahead at all -- so `\u{d83d}\u{de00}`,
#   and both MIXED spellings, decoded to two U+FFFD. Go REJECTED documents
#   TypeScript accepted, the opposite direction from the rest of #24.
#   Fixed in @tabnas/parser 0.8.4 by pairing on the decoded code unit
#   sequence rather than per escape spelling, and it now has real rows
#   (scalar.tsv `surrogate-*`), which is where a resolved behaviour goes.
#   The LONE-SURROGATE half was never a bug upstream -- it is deliberate
#   there -- and the question was whether aontu should refuse an unpaired
#   surrogate in BOTH ports to restore the lattice law. DECLINED
#   (2026-08-11 morning): a documented divergence was judged the smaller
#   cost, and the entry left this file as ACCEPTED, recorded in
#   DIVERGENCE.md.
#   REVERSED the same day: by maintainer decision the divergence is not
#   acceptable and must be fixed. #24 is reopened and the case is OPEN
#   again -- see its live entry ABOVE, which supersedes this note. This
#   closed entry stays only for the braced-spelling half's history.
# The other entry this file has carried is CLOSED; what it recorded is
# kept below, because how it was closed is the part worth remembering.
# CLOSED -- integer-kind values above 2^53 that need more than 17
#   significant digits to write exactly. issue: #21.
#   TypeScript held an integer-kind peg as a JS number and rendered it
#   with Number.toString, which emits the SHORTEST decimal that parses
#   back to the same double. Go held it as an int64 and printed the true
#   value. So 2^60 was `1152921504606847000` in one port and
#   `1152921504606846976` in the other -- two different integers that
#   happen to round to the same double.
#   The entry twice recorded a resolution that turned out to be wrong:
#   that the number tower's D7 (a lossy integer literal is refused)
#   would remove the divergence by refusing the inputs. It does not. D7
#   refuses a literal binary64 cannot carry EXACTLY; it does not refuse
#   one that is merely large, and every value in this window (2^60,
#   2^63-1024) is exactly representable. THE RULE IS EXACTNESS, NOT
#   MAGNITUDE -- the same misreading, in three separate places, that the
#   Phase 6 spec rows had to correct for the hex literals.
#   That mistake is the reason this note survives the entry. A ledger
#   entry closed against a plausible-sounding phase that does not
#   actually touch it looks exactly like a closed entry, and the only
#   thing that caught it both times was re-probing BOTH CLIs at the
#   exact inputs written down here -- which is why rule 3 above demands
#   they be written down.
#   What actually closed it: once D7 landed, every remaining divergent
#   case was one where BOTH ports held exactly the value the source
#   asked for, so "agreeing on the text would only agree on a wrong
#   number" stopped being true. There was a right answer, and Go already
#   printed it. TypeScript now renders an integer-kind value by its
#   exact digits in BOTH places -- IntegerVal.canon, and generate(),
#   which past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER hands back a `bigint` so the
#   exact-JSON emitter can write the digits (JSON.stringify of the JS
#   number reproduces the very 17-digit form canon had just dropped, so
#   the emitter had to be part of the fix). The window is pinned by real
#   rows now: number-tower.tsv, `EXACT INTEGER RENDERING` for canon and
#   `gens-exact-int-*` for the bytes, both routes in -- literal and
#   exact sum.
# NOT recorded here, because they are already documented as deliberate,
# permanent non-parity in AGENTS.md ("Known TS/Go divergences"): error
# MESSAGE text, parse-level (non-unify) canon, the canon of sources that
# are invalid in both ports, and the malformed-input acceptance edges.
# Only the substring an err-mode spec row asserts is contractual.
# Also not a divergence, though it is a difference: the NATIVE TYPE an
# integer generates as. Go returns an int64 at every magnitude;
# TypeScript returns a `number` up to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and a
# `bigint` above it, because its leaf is a double and a double past that
# line no longer renders its own digits. The serialised BYTES agree --
# that is what the gens rows pin -- and the difference is forced by the
# storage, not chosen. It is pinned per-port instead: ts/test/
# exactjson.test.ts and go/generate_test.go.
# OPEN -- Go names a document for a value NOBODY WROTE.
#   issue: #76 (2026-08-25). Found by the parity probe for
#   `aontu set --in-place`. THE INCLUDED-FILE HALF OF THIS IS #66 ABOVE,
#   recorded a week earlier and rediscovered here -- which is the exact
#   failure this ledger exists to prevent, and is left visible rather
#   than tidied away. What follows is the half #66 does not cover.
#   A value MINTED during unification -- `x |> upper` resolving to
#   "HELLO", `1+2` resolving to 3 -- is unsited in both ports (row, col,
#   len and src all agree at -1/-1/-1/empty), but Go names the entry
#   document for it where TypeScript names none.
#   Divergent input:  entry `x: string`, overlay `x: hello |> upper`,
#                     then `set '$.x="BYE"' --in-place --format json`
#   TypeScript: site file = ""        (nobody wrote this value)
#   Go:         site file = <overlay> (the document being stamped)
#   Everything else about the run agrees byte for byte, the written
#   file included.
#   Not simply fixed, and NOT SETTLED BY FIXING #66. TypeScript's
#   distinction is "stamped BEFORE the fixpoint" -- a parsed value,
#   which belongs to its document even when it has no position within it
#   (vet-unsited-junction pins exactly that, and is correct) -- versus
#   "minted DURING it". Go does not track when a value came into being,
#   so stampURL cannot draw the line: guarding it on the `unsited`
#   sentinel was tried and breaks vet-unsited-junction. Knowing WHICH
#   file a value came from, which is what #66 needs, is not the same as
#   knowing whether it came from a file AT ALL -- and the two fixes
#   point in OPPOSITE directions: #66 carries a url further, this one
#   withholds one. TypeScript names a file for #66's value (the right
#   one) and no file for this one; only THIS entry is a case of
#   "TypeScript names none".
#   Reaches `set --in-place` among other reports, and SAFETY IS
#   UNAFFECTED there: the overlay-alone evaluation refuses to edit a
#   document that loads anything, so no attribution question arises
#   before a write.
# OPEN -- a finding inside a value that arrived by a reference to a
#   DEEPER target is reported at a path that does not exist, in
#   TypeScript only.
#   issue: none filed yet; found 2026-08-27 while landing the money wire
#   convention (use-cases/REVIEW.md finding I), by running both engines
#   on the same document and diffing.
#   The trigger is a DEPTH MISMATCH between the reference and its
#   target, not the kind of finding: TypeScript's clone overlays the
#   referring path onto the target's, so a target one level deeper than
#   the referring field leaves exactly one stale segment behind. At
#   EQUAL depth the two ports agree, which is what the two rows
#   vet-ref-clone-names-the-key-not-the-record and
#   vet-type-alias-names-the-key-not-the-record in vet.tsv pin, and why
#   use-cases/10-data-model/money-wire.aon declares its types at the top
#   level rather than under a `schema:` namespace.
#   Divergent input:  schema `schema:{M:type(close({a:string&re("^x$")}))}`
#                     `quote: $.schema.M`
#     with data `{"quote":{}}`         -- an unsatisfied key
#     TypeScript: mapval_required at $.quote.M.a   (no such path in
#                 either document -- the alias's own key is in the tail)
#     Go:         mapval_required at $.quote.a     (correct)
#     with data `{"quote":{"a":"y"}}`  -- a conflict, same shape
#     TypeScript: constraint at $.quote.M.a
#     Go:         constraint at $.quote.a
#   The nil's own path is already taken from the driving context where
#   that EXTENDS the operand's path (use-cases/BUGS.md §41), which fixes
#   the equal-depth case; it deliberately does not redirect a path that
#   is merely wrong, because taking the context path unconditionally was
#   tried and moves every closed-key, spread-template and `--at`
#   finding to the driving location instead.
#   Not simply fixed because the cause is the clone-path difference
#   ts/src/val/RefVal.ts documents in detectRefCycle: Go's
#   clonePath/overlayPath re-paths a resolved clone to the referring
#   site, TypeScript's clone keeps the source paths. Rebasing the clone
#   with the existing repathInstance walk (the spread-instance
#   operation) is NOT the same operation and was tried and reverted: it
#   moves RELATIVE references with it, so
#   `match(.side_effect, destructive, true, false)` in
#   use-cases/09-agent-tools/registry.aon resolves against the
#   destination and dies no_path. The real fix is a TypeScript twin of
#   Go's cloneAt/overlayPath -- a clone that takes a destination path --
#   which is wider than any one finding and is the arm-for-arm
#   correspondence ADR-001 asks for.
# CLOSED 2026-08-30 by ADR-013 -- Go's DERIVED GRAPH loses most of its
#   edges on a two-view
#   id-merged model, so `relations` silently misses a real cycle and
#   `reaches` would under-answer with it.
#   issue: none filed yet; found 2026-08-27 while landing the relations
#   work (use-cases/REVIEW.md finding J), by running use case 01's
#   check.sh through the GO CLI -- which nothing had done, because
#   use-cases/run-all.sh drives the TypeScript one. NOT introduced by
#   that work: the pre-change Go binary loses the same edges.
#   Divergent input:  use-cases/01-service-catalog/system.aon (and
#     bad/cycle.aon, which includes it) -- eight entities described by
#     TWO views (catalog.aon, deploy.aon) joined by id(), with the link
#     lists typed by a spread from a shared vocabulary.
#   TypeScript: graphOf gives 40 edges (19 distinct from/key/to
#               triples); `relations bad/cycle.aon` reports
#               `cycle svc_payments -> svc_ledger -> svc_payments`.
#   Go:         GraphOf gives 6 edges (2 distinct triples); `relations
#               bad/cycle.aon` reports NO cycle, and reports extra
#               inverse_missing findings for the inverses it cannot
#               see. Both ports find the same 8 ENTITIES.
#   What is established: BOTH VIEWS ARE NEEDED. With `deploy: {}` the
#   two ports agree exactly (21 edges each); with one catalog domain
#   and the full deploy they differ by 4. So the trigger is the
#   id-merge across two trees, not the include, the spread or the
#   vocabulary -- each of which agrees on its own. The missing edges
#   are all links the merge carried into a position other than the one
#   they were written at.
#   Not simply fixed because the cause is in how each port's identity
#   merge places a link-stamped value at an entity's other positions,
#   which is engine work rather than a graph-walk fix, and it did not
#   minimise: every synthetic reduction tried (two views + spread, two
#   views + include, an entity in one view pointing at one in two)
#   agrees in both ports. The reproduction is the use case itself,
#   which is in the tree.
#   Guarded meanwhile: use-cases/01-service-catalog/check.sh asserted
#   the cycle, so the Go CLI failed that check rather than passing it
#   quietly -- which is how the fix was noticed.
#   FIXED by removing the cause. The divergence was in "how each port's
#   identity merge places a link-stamped value at an entity's other
#   positions"; ADR-013 removes the identity merge, so there are no
#   other positions and a link is stamped where it is written. Both
#   ports now report the same cycle over the same edge set, and
#   `AONTU=<go binary> check.sh` passes all 20 assertions.
# CLOSED 2026-08-30 by ADR-013 -- an id-spread refusal is pathed at `$`
#   by TypeScript and at `$.&` by Go.
#   issue: none filed yet; found 2026-08-27 while fixing the crash the
#   same document caused (use-cases/BUGS.md 43). PRE-EXISTING and
#   engine-level: plain evaluation disagrees the same way, so it is not
#   the verbs' doing.
#   Divergent input:  `&: id(root)` `b: id(b) & {n: 1}`
#   TypeScript: [aontu/id_spread] Cannot resolve value at path $
#   Go:         [aontu/id_spread] Cannot resolve value at path $.&
#   Was not simply fixed because it is a question about where a bag
#   spread's own refusal SITS -- at the bag, or at the `&` entry that
#   carries it -- which is a language answer rather than a port
#   difference, and neither port was obviously right.
#   MOOT since ADR-013: `id_spread` was clearing rule 3, and the rule
#   existed only to stop one global name being stamped on every child
#   of a bag. With no global names there is no rule and no code. The
#   SHAPE the divergence was about -- a nil root carrying no collected
#   error -- still exists and is still guarded: `&:` alone (an elided
#   spread value) produces it, and the per-port tests named in BUGS.md
#   43 now drive that instead. They still assert the verdict, the code
#   and the exit, and deliberately not the path.
# OPEN -- the SITE of a MERGED CONTAINER that the meet minted: sited by
#   TypeScript at the schema's own brace, unsited by Go.
#   issue: none filed yet; found 2026-08-27 while pinning the sizing
#   soundness fix (use-cases/BUGS.md 16), by probing a row through both
#   library forms and diffing.
#   Divergent input:  schema `x: length(min(2)) & { &: {r: integer} }`,
#   TypeScript: the finding's schema site is len 1, src "{"
#   Go:         the same site is len -1, src "" (unsited)
#   Everything else agrees: verdict `incomplete`, code `constraint`,
#   path `$.x`, expected and actual, and the OTHER site.
#   Not simply fixed because it is the same question the existing
#   `vet-minted-arith-operand-unsited` row settles the other way for a
#   minted SCALAR -- a value the meet built has no source text of its
#   own, and Go says so while TypeScript lends it the brace of the
#   fragment it grew from. Which is right is a finding-F decision about
#   what a site MEANS for a value nobody wrote, and it wants answering
#   once for every minted value rather than per shape.
#   The SAME divergence shows in a finding's PATH, not just its site,
#   and reaches `--at`: anchoring ON a residuated container
#   (`x: length(min(2)) & {a: 1}` with `--at $.x`) has TypeScript report
#   the conflict at `$` and Go at `$.x`, because the path is taken from
#   whichever operand's location wins and TypeScript has re-pathed the
#   merged container to the meet position. Both ports still answer
#   `invalid`, so the SOUNDNESS agrees; only where they say it is
#   differs. Anchoring THROUGH a residue to a child (`--at $.x.a`)
#   agrees byte for byte, and is pinned by
#   `vet-at-steps-through-a-sizing-residue`.
#   The soundness this shape was probed for is pinned instead by
#   `vet-sizing-min-still-short-in-the-data`,
#   `vet-sizing-min-met-by-the-data` and
#   `vet-sizing-min-survives-beside-a-container` in vet.tsv, whose
#   containers the meet does not mint and which both ports agree on byte
#   for byte.
